name: iris_vpu_boot_firmware
prose: Precondition: core points to an initialised iris_core with a valid register base (core->reg_base) and device (core->dev); the function itself sets up the uc-region memory map, so no earlier setup is required. Postcondition: it calls iris_vpu_setup_ucregion_memory_map(core), writes BIT(0) to CTRL_INIT and 0x1 to CPU_CS_SCIACMDARG3, then loops while CTRL_STATUS read as zero and fewer than 1000 iterations have run: each iteration reads CTRL_STATUS; if (status & CTRL_ERROR_STATUS__M) equals 0x4 it logs 'invalid setting for uc_region' and leaves the loop without counting that iteration; otherwise it sleeps 50-100 us and counts the iteration. If the count reaches 1000 it logs an error and returns -ETIME; this happens when no error status 0x4 was seen in any of the 1000 iterations, whatever value the 1000th read returned (a non-zero read still counts and sleeps before the loop test), and it covers the case where CTRL_STATUS stayed zero for all polls. Otherwise (a non-zero status within the first 999 polls, or the error status 0x4 on any of the 1000 reads) it writes HOST2XTENSA_INTR_ENABLE to CPU_CS_H2XSOFTINTEN and 0x0 to CPU_CS_X2RPMH and returns 0; in particular the 0x4 uc_region error is only logged and the function still returns 0. It takes no locks.
note: Reviewer 1 right (error status 0x4 breaks the loop and the function returns 0, iris_vpu_common.c:125-127 and 139-142). Reviewer 3 wrong: the 1000th read does not matter because count is incremented after the sleep even for a non-zero, non-error read (130-131), so the loop ends with count == 1000 and -ETIME (134-137) whenever 1000 iterations complete without the 0x4 break. iris_vpu_boot_firmware at 114-143.

name: calculate_enc_scratch1_size
prose: Precondition: lcu_size is 16 or 32, num_vpp_pipes is between 1 and 16 (so the shift count num_vpp_pipes - 1 is in 0..15), and the caller guarantees that every u32 intermediate in the body stays below 2^32. Postcondition: returns one u32, the sum of the components listed below plus 1024, where width_lcu_num = ceil(width/lcu_size), height_lcu_num = ceil(height/lcu_size), frame_num_lcu = width_lcu_num*height_lcu_num, width_coded = width_lcu_num*lcu_size, height_coded = height_lcu_num*lcu_size, num_lcu_mb = (height_coded/lcu_size)*(width_coded/lcu_size + 8) and bit_depth = 10 when ten_bit else 8: slice_info_bufsize = ALIGN(256 + 16*frame_num_lcu, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); line_buf_ctrl_size and line_buf_ctrl_size_buffid2, each ALIGN(width_coded, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); line_buf_data_size = ALIGN(bit_depth*width_coded + 1024, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT) + 2*ALIGN((bit_depth*width_coded + 1024)/2, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); leftline_buf_ctrl_size = (height_coded + 32)/32*64 when is_h265 else (height_coded + 15)/16*80, then plus 512 and ALIGN(..., 512)*num_vpp_pipes when num_vpp_pipes > 1, then ALIGN(..., HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); vpss_line_buf = ((max(width_coded, height_coded) + 3)/4*32 + 256)*16 + 65536*num_vpp_pipes + 64; col_mv_buf_size = ALIGN(16*(4*frame_num_lcu + 32) when is_h265 else 48*(frame_num_lcu + 32), HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT)*(num_ref + 1); topline_buf_ctrl_size_FE = ALIGN(64*(width_coded/32), HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT) when is_h265 else ALIGN(HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT + 16*(width_coded/16), HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); leftline_buf_ctrl_size_FE = (HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT + 64*(height_coded/16)) rounded up to a multiple of (HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT << (num_vpp_pipes - 1)), times num_vpp_pipes; line_buf_recon_pix_size = ALIGN((ten_bit ? 3 : 2)*width_coded, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); leftline_buf_recon_pix_size = ((ten_bit + 1)*2*height_coded + HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT) rounded up to a multiple of (HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT << (num_vpp_pipes - 1)); leftline_buf_meta_recony = ALIGN(HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT + 64*(height_coded/(8*(ten_bit ? 4 : 8))), HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT)*num_vpp_pipes; linebuf_meta_recon_uv = ALIGN(HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT + 64*(height_coded/(4*(ten_bit ? 4 : 8))), HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT)*num_vpp_pipes; h265e_colrcbuf_size = ((width_lcu_num + 7)/8)*32*height_lcu_num, then ALIGN(..., HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT)*num_vpp_pipes when num_vpp_pipes > 1, then ALIGN(..., HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT)*HFI_MAX_COL_FRAME; h265e_framerc_bufsize = (256 + 16*(14 + (height_coded/32 + 7)/8)) when is_h265 else (256 + 16*(14 + (height_coded/16 + 7)/8)), times 6, then ALIGN(..., HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT)*num_vpp_pipes when num_vpp_pipes > 1, then ALIGN(..., 512)*HFI_MAX_COL_FRAME; h265e_lcubitcnt_bufsize = ALIGN(256 + 4*frame_num_lcu, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); h265e_lcubitmap_bufsize = ALIGN(256 + frame_num_lcu/8, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); line_buf_sde_size = ALIGN(256 + 16*(width_coded/16), HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); topline_bufsize_fe_1stg_sao = ALIGN(16*(width_coded/32), HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); override_buffer_size = ALIGN(16*((num_lcu_mb + 7)/8), HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT)*2; bse_slice_cmd_buffer_size = 196608; bse_reg_buffer_size = 16384; vpp_reg_buffer_size = ((HFI_VENUS_VPPSG_MAX_REGISTERS*8 + 31) & ~31)*10; sps_pps_slice_hdr = 6144; slice_cmd_buffer_size = ALIGN(20480, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT); ir_buffer_size = ((2*frame_num_lcu + 7) & ~7)*3; lambda_lut_size = 2816; and se_stats_bufsize = 0 when width_coded*height_coded > 4096*2160, ALIGN(160*frame_num_lcu + 512, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT)*2 when width_coded*height_coded > 1920*1088, and ALIGN(1024*frame_num_lcu + 512, HFI_DMA_ALIGNMENT)*2 otherwise; the result is therefore always at least 1024. The call acquires or releases no locks, references or memory.
note: Verified every component of the sum against hfi_plat_bufs_v6.c:772-905 line by line (slice info, line buffers, left line buffer with the num_vpp_pipes > 1 path, vpss line buffer 65536*pipes + 64, col_mv for h265 16*(4*n+32) and h264 48*(n+32), colrc, framerc, bit count/bitmap, SDE, stats thresholds 4096*2160 and 1920*1088, bse/vpp/slice/ir/lambda constants, + 1024). name: ubwc_metadata_plane_stride
prose: Precondition: tile_width_pels and metadata_stride_multi are positive, metadata_stride_multi is a power of two (so the bitwise ALIGN rounds up to a true multiple), and the intermediate values width + tile_width_pels - 1 and (width + tile_width_pels - 1)/tile_width_pels + metadata_stride_multi - 1 fit in u32 without overflow. Postcondition: returns the number of tile columns needed to cover width, ceil(width/tile_width_pels), rounded up to the next multiple of metadata_stride_multi; no locks, references or memory are acquired or released.
contract: /*@ requires tile_width_pels > 0 && metadata_stride_multi > 0 && ((metadata_stride_multi & (metadata_stride_multi - 1)) == 0) && width + tile_width_pels <= 4294967296 && (width + tile_width_pels - 1) / tile_width_pels + metadata_stride_multi <= 4294967296; ensures result == (((width + tile_width_pels - 1) / tile_width_pels + metadata_stride_multi - 1) / metadata_stride_multi) * metadata_stride_multi; */
note: Matches hfi_plat_bufs_v6.c:928-933 (ALIGN(ceil(width/tile), multi)); ALIGN is mask-based so the power-of-two requirement in the prose and contract is correct. Prose and contract unchanged.

Postcondition: returns the number of tile rows needed to cover height, ceil(height/tile_height_pels), rounded up to the next multiple of metadata_height_multi; no locks, references or memory are acquired or released.
contract: /*@ requires tile_height_pels > 0 && metadata_height_multi > 0 && ((metadata_height_multi & (metadata_height_multi - 1)) == 0) && height + tile_height_pels <= 4294967296 && (height + tile_height_pels - 1) / tile_height_pels + metadata_height_multi <= 4294967296; ensures result == (((height + tile_height_pels - 1) / tile_height_pels + metadata_height_multi - 1) / metadata_height_multi) * metadata_height_multi; */

name: enc_scratch2_size
prose: Precondition: the caller guarantees that every u32 intermediate in either branch, including the final multiplication by num_ref + 3, stays below 2^32. Postcondition: returns one u32 equal to (per-reference size)*(num_ref + 3) + 4096, hence always at least 4096; the per-reference size is, when ten_bit is false, (ALIGN(height, HFI_VENUS_HEIGHT_ALIGNMENT) + ALIGN(height/2, HFI_VENUS_HEIGHT_ALIGNMENT)) * ALIGN(width, HFI_VENUS_WIDTH_ALIGNMENT) plus two NV12-UBWC metadata buffer sizes, each ALIGN(metadata_stride * meta_buf_height, SZ_4K) with metadata_stride = ALIGN(ceil(width/NV12_UBWC_Y_TILE_WIDTH), 64) and meta_buf_height = ALIGN(ceil(height/NV12_UBWC_Y_TILE_HEIGHT), 16); and when ten_bit is true, the 4K-aligned TP10 luma size ALIGN(height, HFI_VENUS_HEIGHT_ALIGNMENT) * ref_stride plus the 4K-aligned chroma size ref_stride * ALIGN(ceil(height/2), 32), where ref_stride = 4*(ceil(width/SYSTEM_LAL_TILE10)*SYSTEM_LAL_TILE10/3) rounded up to a multiple of 128, plus two TP10-UBWC metadata buffer sizes, each ALIGN(metadata_stride * meta_buf_height, SZ_4K) with metadata_stride = ALIGN(ceil(width/TP10_UBWC_Y_TILE_WIDTH), METADATA_STRIDE_MULTIPLE) and meta_buf_height = ALIGN(ceil(height/TP10_UBWC_Y_TILE_HEIGHT), METADATA_HEIGHT_MULTIPLE). The call acquires or releases no locks, references or memory.
note: Checked both branches of enc_scratch2_size (hfi_plat_bufs_v6.c:948-1008) against the prose: non-10-bit uses aligned heights/width plus two UBWC metadata planes (stride multiple 64, height multiple 16), 10-bit uses the TP10 stride from SYSTEM_LAL_TILE10 and 4K-aligned luma/chroma plus two metadata planes, then (size*(num_ref+3))+4096 in both. ubwc_metadata_plane_buffer_size = ALIGN(stride*height, SZ_4K) (942-946). Removed the unverifiable claim about caller values.

name: venc_v4l2_to_hfi
prose: Precondition: none; id and value may be any ints. Postcondition: it returns 2 (HFI_H264_ENTROPY_CABAC) when id is V4L2_CID_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_ENTROPY_MODE (0x00990A65) and value is V4L2_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_ENTROPY_MODE_CABAC (1), and 1 (HFI_H264_ENTROPY_CAVLC) for any other value of that control. When id is V4L2_CID_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_LOOP_FILTER_MODE (0x00990A6A) it returns 1 (HFI_H264_DB_MODE_DISABLE) for value V4L2_MPEG_VIDEO_H264_LOOP_FILTER_MODE_DISABLED (1), 2 (HFI_H264_DB_MODE_SKIP_SLICE_BOUNDARY) for value ..._DISABLED_AT_SLICE_BOUNDARY (2), and 3 (HFI_H264_DB_MODE_ALL_BOUNDARY) for every other value, including ENABLED (0). For any other id it returns 0. It reads no state, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires 	rue; ensures (id == 0x00990A65 ? (value == 1 ? result == 2 : result == 1) : (id == 0x00990A6A ? (value == 1 ? result == 1 : (value == 2 ? result == 2 : result == 3)) : result == 0)); */

So reviewer 1 right (HFI constants misnumbered) and reviewer 3 right that the IDs were wrong (but its replacement values are also wrong). venc.c:118-142.

name: rcsi2_start_receiver_gen3
prose: Precondition: priv is an initialised rcar_csi2 device and state is a valid subdev state whose sink-pad (RCAR_CSI2_SINK) format is available; the format code is expected to have been validated by set_fmt. Postcondition: this is rcsi2_start_receiver_gen3. It returns -EINVAL, before writing any register, if rcsi2_code_to_fmt cannot map the sink format code. It builds the VCDT and VCDT2 words from the channels whose channel_vc entry is not negative (channels 0 and 1 go into VCDT, higher channels into VCDT2) with the data type of the format, and the FLD word when the sink field is V4L2_FIELD_ALTERNATE. It returns the negative error of rcsi2_get_active_lanes if the active lane count cannot be determined, and the negative result of rcsi2_calc_mbps if the bit rate cannot be computed, still before any register write. It then enables the interrupts, writes TREF and PHTC, writes VCDT (and VCDT2 only when it is non-zero) only if info->use_isp is false, writes the lane swap register from priv->lane_swap, and runs the platform steps: init_phtw(priv, mbps) if present, rcsi2_set_phypll if info->hsfreqrange is set (each returning its non-zero error at once), the CSI0 clock frequency range if info->csi0clkfreqrange is set, and the force-RX bits if info->use_isp is set. It writes PHYCNT, LINKCNT, FLD and then PHYCNT with SHUTDOWNZ and RSTZ, and waits with rcsi2_wait_phy_start for the PHY to start (returning its error), clears the force-RX register if info->use_isp, runs info->phy_post_init if present (returning its error), and clears the ULPS interrupt state if info->clear_ulps is set. It returns 0 at the end. On an error after the first register write earlier register writes are not undone. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is rcsi2_start_receiver_gen3 (rcar-csi2.c:1038-1187), not a function named rcsi2_start_receiver; the v4h and v4m variants are separate functions. Old prose was correct about the error returns but described the register writes as happening only 'on success' and omitted that the three validation returns come before any write. Mechanical reviewer right on the name.

name: vsp1_uif_create
prose: Precondition: vsp1 points to a valid vsp1_device (vsp1->dev usable) and index is a UIF instance number; the 6-byte name buffer fits "uif.N" only for a single-digit index + 4 (that is, index at most 5). Postcondition: this is vsp1_uif_create. It allocates the vsp1_uif with devm_kzalloc on vsp1->dev and returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if that fails. It sets uif->m3w_quirk to true if soc_device_match finds the r8a7796 SoC, sets uif->entity.ops, type VSP1_ENTITY_UIF and index, formats the name "uif.<index + 4>" and calls vsp1_entity_init with 2 pads and the uif operations (MEDIA_ENT_F_PROC_VIDEO_STATISTICS). If vsp1_entity_init returns a negative value it returns ERR_PTR of that value (the devm allocation is not freed here; it lives until the device is released); otherwise it returns uif.
note: Not a drop: the slice 254-262 is the body of vsp1_uif_create (vsp1_uif.c:234-262 region); real name used and the old prose's 'initialised entity' wording kept but made precise (ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM), quirk flag, name formatting, devm ownership).

name: s5p_mfc_set_enc_params_hevc
prose: Precondition: ctx points to an initialised MFC context for HEVC encoding whose ctx->dev, register map (dev->mfc_regs) and enc_params (the HEVC parameters in ctx->enc_params.codec.hevc and the shared num_b_frame, rc_frame and rc_mb) have been set by the caller. Postcondition: this is s5p_mfc_set_enc_params_hevc. It first calls s5p_mfc_set_enc_params(ctx) (its result is ignored) for the common parameters, then writes the B-frame count into bits 16-17 of e_gop_config. If ctx->img_width is 3840 and ctx->img_height is 2160 it sets p_hevc->level to 51 and p_hevc->tier to 0. It writes profile (2 bits), level and tier into e_picture_profile. By p_hevc->loopfilter it sets p_hevc->loopfilter_disable to 1 (DISABLED, loopfilter_across unchanged), or loopfilter_disable 0 and loopfilter_across 1 (ENABLED), or loopfilter_disable 0 and loopfilter_across 0 (DISABLED_AT_SLICE_BOUNDARY); any other value leaves both unchanged. It packs the HEVC option bits (partition depth, num_refs_for_p - 1, refresh type, intra and CU options, loop filter bits, LTR, hierarchical QP, temporal id and so on) into e_hevc_options. It then writes the refresh period only if p_hevc->refreshtype is non-zero, the loop-filter beta and tc offsets only if loopfilter_disable is 0, and, only if p_hevc->num_hier_layer is non-zero, e_num_t_layer, plus the seven per-layer QP registers if hier_qp_enable is set and the seven per-layer bit-rate registers if p->rc_frame is set. It always updates e_rc_config (macroblock-level rate control bit and the frame QP, with two writes), writes e_rc_frame_rate only if p->rc_frame is set, always writes e_rc_qp_bound, writes 0 to e_fixed_picture_qp and, only if both p->rc_frame and p->rc_mb are 0, writes the B, P and frame QPs there. It always returns 0, takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is s5p_mfc_set_enc_params_hevc (s5p_mfc_opr_v6.c:1594-1857), not s5p_mfc_init_encode_hevc_v6 (the slice also contains following functions). Old prose said it 'conditionally writes' several registers without saying under which conditions; the exact conditions are listed here, and it did not mention the ignored call to s5p_mfc_set_enc_params or that loopfilter_across is unchanged for the DISABLED mode. Mechanical reviewer right on the name.

name: omap_vout_prepare_vrfb
prose: Precondition: vout points to an initialised omap_vout_device (pix, bpp, vrfb_bpp, vrfb_context, queued_buf_addr and vrfb_dma_tx with its channel, template and wait queue set up), and vb is the vb2 buffer being queued, with vb->index valid for vrfb_context and queued_buf_addr and plane 0 DMA-contiguous. Postcondition: this is omap_vout_prepare_vrfb(vout, vb). If is_rotation_enabled(vout) is false it returns 0 immediately without doing any DMA and without writing vout->queued_buf_addr. Otherwise it fills the interleaved-DMA template (source = the DMA address of plane 0, destination = vrfb_context[vb->index].paddr[0], one frame per line of the image) and calls dmaengine_prep_interleaved_dma; if that returns NULL it prints an error and returns -EINVAL. It sets the completion callback, calls dmaengine_submit and returns -EINVAL (after an error message) if dma_submit_error reports an error; neither of these two error returns terminates the channel. It then clears vrfb_dma_tx.tx_status, issues the pending DMA and waits with wait_event_interruptible_timeout for tx_status to become 1, for at most VRFB_TX_TIMEOUT. After the wait it reads the transaction status; if tx_status is still 0 (timeout or interrupted wait) it prints an error, calls dmaengine_terminate_sync(chan) and returns -EINVAL; otherwise, if the status is not DMA_COMPLETE it prints an error, calls dmaengine_terminate_sync(chan) and returns -EINVAL. On success it stores vrfb_context[vb->index].paddr[calc_rotation(vout)] into vout->queued_buf_addr[vb->index] and returns 0. The DMA engine owns the submitted descriptor; the function holds no lock and keeps no reference to it.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is omap_vout_prepare_vrfb(vout, vb) (omap_vout_vrfb.c:230-316), which takes no chan, buf_phy_addr or flags arguments (the old prose invented them). The old prose also missed the early return 0 when rotation is not enabled (line 248-249, no DMA and queued_buf_addr untouched). Mechanical reviewer right on the name.

name: xtpg_parse_of
prose: Precondition: xtpg points to an initialised xtpg_device whose xvip.dev and xvip.dev->of_node are valid; xtpg->vip_format is NULL on the first call (if it is already non-NULL, every port format must equal it). Postcondition: it iterates over the graph ports of the device node. For each port it obtains the video format with xvip_of_get_format and returns PTR_ERR of an error format at once (after logging 'invalid format in DT'); it sets xtpg->vip_format to the format if it was NULL, and returns -EINVAL (after logging) if a later port has a different format than xtpg->vip_format; for the first port only it checks whether the port has an endpoint, remembering the result and putting the endpoint node reference immediately. It counts the ports. After the loop it returns -EINVAL if the count is neither 1 nor 2. Otherwise it sets xtpg->npads to the count, sets xtpg->has_input to true only when there are two ports and the first port has an endpoint (otherwise has_input is not written), and returns 0. On the error returns xtpg->npads and xtpg->has_input are not assigned, but xtpg->vip_format may already have been set. The port node reference held by the loop variable is released automatically on every exit, including the early returns, because for_each_of_graph_port declares the loop variable with __free(device_node); no other reference is kept.
note: Reviewer 3 wrong: for_each_of_graph_port (of_graph.h:49-51) declares the loop variable with __free(device_node), so an early return from inside the loop puts the current port node automatically; the endpoint node is put explicitly (xilinx-tpg.c:740). The old claim that every reference is released was right. The old prose omitted the case where xtpg->vip_format was already set. Function at 711-757.

name: img_ir_probe_raw

name: ir_mce_kbd_decode
prose: Precondition: dev points to a valid rc_dev whose raw->mce_kbd decoder state, rx_timeout timer and keylock are initialized, and ev is the next raw IR event for that device. Postcondition: the function returns 0 leaving the decoder state unchanged when ev is not a timing event and ev.overflow is false, returns 0 with the state set to STATE_INACTIVE when ev is not a timing event and ev.overflow is true, returns -EINVAL with the state set to STATE_INACTIVE when a timing event is shorter than MCIR2_UNIT/2 at entry or when a state handler fails (a space or non-prefix pulse in STATE_INACTIVE, a duration at least MCIR2_MAX_LEN minus MCIR2_UNIT/2 in STATE_HEADER_BIT_START or STATE_BODY_BIT_START, an unrecognized header mode, a pulse in STATE_FINISHED, or an unexpected wanted_bits value), returns 0 with the state set to STATE_HEADER_BIT_START and count and header cleared after a valid prefix pulse in STATE_INACTIVE, returns 0 after shifting in a header or body bit and setting the corresponding *_BIT_END state in STATE_HEADER_BIT_START or STATE_BODY_BIT_START, in STATE_HEADER_BIT_END subtracts MCIR2_BIT_END from the duration and either sets STATE_HEADER_BIT_START and reprocesses when count is not MCIR2_HEADER_NBITS or, when count is MCIR2_HEADER_NBITS and the mode is keyboard or mouse, sets wanted_bits, clears count and body, sets STATE_BODY_BIT_START and reprocesses, in STATE_BODY_BIT_END sets STATE_FINISHED when count equals wanted_bits (otherwise STATE_BODY_BIT_START), subtracts MCIR2_BIT_END and reprocesses, returns 0 after a state transition when the possibly decreased duration is shorter than MCIR2_UNIT/2 (leaving the state as just set), and on a completed keyboard or mouse message returns 0 after passing the scancode to ir_mce_kbd_process_keyboard_data or ir_mce_kbd_process_mouse_data, setting lsc.rc_proto to RC_PROTO_MCIR2_KBD or RC_PROTO_MCIR2_MSE, setting lsc.scancode, emitting a lirc scancode event and an MSC_SCAN input event followed by input_sync, and setting the state to STATE_INACTIVE, with the keyboard case taking and releasing data->keylock and either re-arming data->rx_timeout for dev->timeout plus 100 ms when the scancode is nonzero or deleting it when the scancode is zero.
note: Checked every return and goto against the prose (ir-mce_kbd-decoder.c:217-360). Reviewer 2 right only about the entry check (line 230-231 goes to out: state INACTIVE, -EINVAL), which the prose already stated. Reviewers 1 and 3 wrong about the post-decrease check: the second geq_margin test after the 'again' label (237-238) does 'return 0', not 'goto out', so the state just set is kept and 0 is returned; the prose already said that. Prose unchanged.

name: init_rc_map_msi_tvanywhere_plus
prose: Precondition: module-init context; the static msi_tvanywhere_plus_map list entry must not already be on the rc map list. Postcondition: it returns the value of rc_map_register(&msi_tvanywhere_plus_map). In this source tree rc_map_register takes rc_map_lock, appends the entry to the global keymap list and always returns 0 (it allocates nothing and has no failure path), so the function returns 0 and the keymap stays registered until exit_rc_map_msi_tvanywhere_plus unregisters it with rc_map_unregister. The map data (msi_tvanywhere_plus, with RC_PROTO_UNKNOWN and the name RC_MAP_MSI_TVANYWHERE_PLUS) is static and owned by this module.
note: Old prose and contract were wrong to describe a possible -ENOMEM or a range of negative errnos: rc_map_register (rc-main.c:135-141) only list_add_tail()s under a spinlock and returns 0. Contract left empty because the function modifies a global list (rule 4). init_rc_map_msi_tvanywhere_plus at keymaps/rc-msi-tvanywhere-plus.c (module init function near the end of the file).

name: lirc_transmit
prose: Precondition: file->private_data is a valid lirc_fh whose rc device is valid; the caller does not hold dev->lock; buf is a user pointer to n bytes. Postcondition: this is lirc_transmit (the write handler). It takes dev->lock interruptibly and returns the error (-ERESTARTSYS) if interrupted. Under the lock it returns -ENODEV if the device is not registered and -EINVAL if dev->tx_ir is NULL. In LIRC_MODE_SCANCODE it requires n to equal sizeof(struct lirc_scancode) (else -EINVAL), copies it (-EFAULT on failure), returns -EINVAL if flags, keycode or timestamp are non-zero, rc_proto is above RC_PROTO_MAX, the scancode does not fit 32 bits or fails rc_validate_scancode, allocates a raw-event array (-ENOMEM on failure), encodes the scancode with ir_raw_encode_scancode (a negative result is returned), drops a trailing space so the pulse count is odd, allocates and fills the duration buffer (-ENOMEM on failure) and sets the carrier with dev->s_tx_carrier if present and the protocol has one. In the other mode it requires n to be a non-zero multiple of 4 bytes with an odd count of at most LIRCBUF_SIZE entries (else -EINVAL) and copies the data with memdup_user (its error is returned). It then returns -EINVAL if any duration is zero or the total would exceed IR_MAX_DURATION, and otherwise calls dev->tx_ir(dev, txbuf, count); a negative result is returned. In every failure case it frees the buffers it allocated and releases dev->lock before returning. On success it frees the buffers, releases dev->lock, sleeps interruptibly until the computed signal duration has elapsed (a signal can end this wait early) and returns n; the non-negative return value of tx_ir is not used.
note: Not a drop: the slice is inside lirc_transmit (lirc_dev.c:216-360), the file's write handler; the packet name lirc_write is not a function in this file. The old prose omitted the -ENODEV (not registered) and -EINVAL (no tx_ir) returns and the interruptible final wait. Mechanical reviewer right on the name.

name: vicodec_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is a platform device being probed. Postcondition: kzalloc failure returns -ENOMEM with nothing else done. If v4l2_device_register fails it returns that error after only kfree(dev) (v4l2_device_unregister is not called). Otherwise it sets dev->v4l2_dev.release to vicodec_v4l2_dev_release, and, if CONFIG_MEDIA_CONTROLLER is enabled, fills in and initialises dev->mdev with media_device_init and links it to v4l2_dev; it calls platform_set_drvdata(pdev, dev) and registers three instances with register_instance: stateful-encoder, stateful-decoder and stateless-decoder, each with its video device and m2m context. With CONFIG_MEDIA_CONTROLLER it then registers the media controllers of the three m2m devices (encoder, decoder, stateless decoder) with v4l2_m2m_register_media_controller and calls media_device_register. If all steps succeed it returns 0. On a failure it returns the failing step's negative error and unwinds in reverse order what was created before it: media controllers already registered, then the video devices and m2m contexts of the instances created (video_unregister_device plus v4l2_m2m_release), then v4l2_device_unregister (only for failures after v4l2_device_register succeeded), then kfree(dev). It never calls v4l2_device_put or media_device_cleanup, so vicodec_v4l2_dev_release is not run on an error path and the media_device_init state is not cleaned up, and a failure after platform_set_drvdata leaves the drvdata of pdev pointing at the freed dev. If the first media controller (encoder) fails, the unwind does not unregister any media controller but does unregister all three instances.
note: Reviewer 1 right (no media_device_cleanup after media_device_init on the error paths); reviewer 2 right (the release callback is never reached because dev is kfree'd rather than put); reviewer 3 right (v4l2_device_register failure goes to free_dev, vicodec-core.c:2106-2108, so v4l2_device_unregister is not called then; the old prose said it was called on any later failure and did not separate this first case). vicodec_probe at 2097-2195.

name: vivid_create_instance
prose: Precondition: pdev is the platform device being probed, inst indexes the module-parameter arrays (node_types, ccs_cap_mode, ccs_out_mode, allocators and others) with a valid configuration, and vivid_devs[inst] is not yet set. Postcondition: this is vivid_create_instance. It allocates the vivid_dev with kzalloc; on failure it returns -ENOMEM with nothing allocated or registered (there is nothing to free). It initialises the media device (with CONFIG_MEDIA_CONTROLLER) and registers the v4l2_device; if v4l2_device_register fails it frees dev with kfree and returns that error. Afterwards it sets the release callback to vivid_dev_release; every later failure releases dev through v4l2_device_put (so vivid_dev_release runs) rather than kfree. It then detects the feature set (vivid_detect_feature_set, error returned), allocates the test pattern generator buffers, scaled_line, blended_line (vzalloc) and edid (vmalloc), returning -ENOMEM if any fails, and runs vivid_init_dv_timings (negative result returned); these failures go straight to the v4l2_device_put exit. After setting defaults it calls vivid_create_controls, vivid_create_queues, creates CEC receive and transmit adapters and the CEC kthread when CONFIG_VIDEO_VIVID_CEC is enabled and the device has HDMI inputs or outputs, runs v4l2_ctrl_handler_setup on all handlers (results ignored) and calls vivid_create_devnodes. A failure of vivid_create_controls, vivid_create_queues, vivid_cec_alloc_adap, kthread_run or vivid_create_devnodes goes to the unwind that unregisters all video device nodes, calls cec_unregister_adapter on the receive adapter and on every transmit adapter slot, stops the CEC kthread if it was started, and then does v4l2_device_put and returns that error. On success it sets vivid_devs[inst] to dev and returns 0; on any failure vivid_devs[inst] is not changed.
note: Reviewer right: a kzalloc failure just returns -ENOMEM (vivid-core.c:1814-1816), dev is NULL and nothing is freed; the old prose said dev was freed with kfree in that case. Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is vivid_create_instance (vivid-core.c:1800-2078). I read the whole function. Observation (not stated in prose): when allocating a later CEC transmit adapter fails, the loop deletes the adapters already created with cec_delete_adapter but leaves their pointers in dev->cec_tx_adap[], and the unwind then calls cec_unregister_adapter on those same slots (lines ~1993-2010 and the unreg_dev label).

name: vivid_create_controls
prose: Precondition: dev is a vivid_dev whose feature flags (has_vid_cap, has_vid_out, has_vbi_cap, has_vbi_out, has_radio_rx, has_radio_tx, has_sdr_cap, has_meta_cap, has_meta_out, has_touch_cap, has_fb, num_hdmi_inputs/outputs and so on) and input/output type arrays have been set up by vivid_detect_feature_set; show_ccs_cap, show_ccs_out, no_error_inj, has_sdtv and has_hdmi select optional controls. Postcondition: this is vivid_create_controls. It initialises the user-general, user-video, user-audio, streaming, SDTV-capture, loop-capture, framebuffer, video capture/output, VBI, radio, SDR, metadata and touch control handlers and creates the controls that the device's features call for. It then checks the error field of the user-general, user-video, user-audio, streaming, SDR-capture and loop-capture handlers in that order and returns the first non-zero one. Next, if dev->autogain it sets up the autogain/gain cluster, and for each feature that dev supports (video capture, video output, VBI capture, VBI output, radio RX, radio TX, SDR capture, metadata capture, metadata output, touch capture, in that order) it adds the shared user, audio, streaming and other handlers to that feature's handler, returns that handler's error if non-zero and otherwise sets the corresponding video device's ctrl_handler pointer. The first such error ends the function at once with the handlers created so far left in place (they are released later by vivid_free_controls) and later features not processed; the SDTV-capture and framebuffer handlers have no separate error check. It returns 0 if all checks pass. It takes no locks.
note: Not a drop: the slice 1792-2092 is the tail of vivid_create_controls (vivid-ctrls.c:1631-2099), a real function whose head was cut; the packet name vivid_create_ctrls was not in the file. The old prose ('returning the first handler error or 0') was right but vague. I read the head, all return paths and the tail (handler error checks), and a structural grep of the middle, not every control definition, so the prose says only that features create their controls.

name: MXL_BlockInit
prose: Precondition: fe->tuner_priv points to an initialised mxl5005s_state whose Mode, AGC_Mode, TOP, IF_OUT, IF_OUT_LOAD, Chan_Bandwidth, Mod_Type, EN_RSSI, CLOCK_OUT and DIV_OUT fields hold the requested configuration. Postcondition: this is MXL_BlockInit. It starts with MXL_OverwriteICDefault and then issues a long series of MXL_ControlWrite calls that set the downconverter, baseband filter, low-pass filter band, AGC mode, TOP level, IF output load, IF output and clock output controls according to those state fields, with extra control writes for each Mod_Type (digital DTV, QAM, analog cable, analog over-the-air) and a final group of RSSI-disable writes when state->EN_RSSI is 0. It returns the u16 sum of all the MXL_ControlWrite return values (0 if every call returned 0; the sum wraps modulo 65536). It also changes the state: for Mod_Type MXL_QAM it sets state->Mode to MXL_DIGITAL_MODE, and for MXL_ANALOG_CABLE it sets state->AGC_Mode to 1 (single AGC mode); it takes no locks and allocates nothing. It has no early return and does not stop on the first failure.
note: Not a drop: the slice 1814-2074 is the middle and tail of MXL_BlockInit (mxl5005s.c:1766-2102), a real function whose head was cut. The old prose omitted the state changes (Mode, AGC_Mode) and said writes 'accumulated into the local status variable' without stating the return. I read the head, the Mod_Type tail and a structural grep of the middle (switches on Mode, Chan_Bandwidth, TOP, IF_OUT), not every individual control write.

name: xc4000_set_params
prose: Precondition: fe is a valid dvb_frontend whose tuner_priv points to an initialised xc4000_priv; fe->dtv_property_cache holds the delivery system, frequency and bandwidth_hz. Postcondition: it takes priv->lock and releases it on every return path. It chooses rf_mode, freq_offset, video_standard and firmware type from the delivery system: SYS_ATSC (air, 1750000, DTV6), SYS_DVBC_ANNEX_B (cable, 1750000, DTV6), and SYS_DVBT or SYS_DVBT2 (air) by bandwidth_hz (0 gives DTV7/8 with an offset of 2250000 below 400 MHz or 2750000 otherwise; up to 6 MHz DTV6, up to 7 MHz DTV7, otherwise DTV8). Any other delivery system logs an error and returns -EINVAL before changing any priv field. Otherwise it sets priv->freq_hz = frequency - freq_offset (the rf_mode, freq_offset and video_standard fields have already been written) and calls check_firmware; if that returns non-zero the function returns -EREMOTEIO (the initial value of its return variable, not the error from check_firmware), before setting priv->bandwidth. It then sets priv->bandwidth, calls xc_set_signal_source and returns its error if non-zero. It then calls xc_set_tv_standard and ignores a failure (the goto fail is commented out), writes XREG_D_CODE, and optionally XREG_AMPLITUDE and XREG_SMOOTHEDCVBS; a failure of those register writes only produces an error message and does not make the function fail. It then calls xc_tune_channel(priv, priv->freq_hz) (result ignored) and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 4 wrong: the 'goto fail' after xc_set_tv_standard failing and after the register-write failures is commented out (xc4000.c:1221-1223 and 1239-1242), and ret is reset to 0 at line 1246, so those failures are ignored. Old prose wrong about check_firmware: its failure jumps to fail with ret still at the initial -EREMOTEIO (1143, 1202-1203). Slice cut the head. Function at 1136-1252.

name: xc5000_set_digital_params
prose: Precondition: fe, fe->tuner_priv and fe->dtv_property_cache are valid, with bandwidth_hz, frequency and delivery_system populated. Postcondition: it first calls xc_load_fw_and_init_tuner(fe, 0) and returns -EINVAL, changing no priv field, if that returns non-zero. It then sets priv fields by delivery system: SYS_ATSC gives XC_RF_MODE_AIR, freq_offset 1750000, video_standard DTV6; SYS_DVBC_ANNEX_B gives XC_RF_MODE_CABLE, 1750000, DTV6; for SYS_ISDBT (a bandwidth of 0 is treated as 6000000), SYS_DMBTH, SYS_DVBT and SYS_DVBT2 it gives XC_RF_MODE_AIR with DTV6 and 1750000 for 6000000, DTV7 and 2250000 for 7000000, DTV8 and 2750000 for 8000000, and any other bandwidth returns -EINVAL (with priv->video_standard, freq_offset and rf_mode not yet written for that call); for SYS_DVBC_ANNEX_A and SYS_DVBC_ANNEX_C it gives XC_RF_MODE_CABLE with DTV6/1750000 up to 6 MHz, DTV7/2250000 up to 7 MHz and DTV7_8/2750000 above; any other delivery system returns -EINVAL. It then sets priv->freq_hz to the frequency minus freq_offset and priv->mode to V4L2_TUNER_DIGITAL_TV, and returns the result of xc5000_tune_digital(fe): 0 on success, -EREMOTEIO if setting the signal source or TV standard fails, or -EIO if setting the IF frequency fails (the OUTPUT_AMP write and the tune call themselves are not checked).
note: Reviewer 1 right (firmware load first, -EINVAL on failure); reviewer 2 right (the return is that of xc5000_tune_digital, which can fail); reviewer 3 right (SYS_ATSC sets XC_RF_MODE_AIR, xc5000.c:742-747; the old prose lumped ATSC with CABLE). I read xc5000_tune_digital (683-724) to give its error codes. xc5000_set_digital_params at 726-815.

name: au0828_irq_callback
prose: Precondition: urb is a completed isochronous URB whose context points to the au0828_dmaqueue (vidq) embedded in an initialised au0828_dev whose isoc_ctl.isoc_copy callback is valid. Postcondition: if urb->status is -ECONNRESET, -ENOENT or -ESHUTDOWN it logs and returns immediately without copying, resetting descriptors, resubmitting the URB or changing dev->stream_state. For any other status (0, -ETIMEDOUT and other errors, which are only logged) it calls dev->isoc_ctl.isoc_copy(dev, urb) with dev->slock held (spin_lock_irqsave) and releases the lock, sets status and actual_length of each of the urb->number_of_packets frame descriptors to 0, sets urb->status to 0 and then to the return value of usb_submit_urb(urb, GFP_ATOMIC), logs if that is non-zero, and finally sets dev->stream_state to STREAM_ON whether or not the resubmission succeeded. A successful resubmission hands the URB back to the USB core; if usb_submit_urb fails the URB is not freed or otherwise handled here. The function returns nothing.
note: Reviewer 1 right in itself (the kill statuses return early; the old prose already said so); reviewer 3 right: the URB is resubmitted with usb_submit_urb (au0828-video.c:143), so after a successful submit it belongs to the USB core, not 'stays with the caller'. au0828_irq_callback at 110-149.

name: cx231xx_register_analog_devices
prose: Precondition: dev points to an initialised cx231xx device (model, tuner_type, devno, lock, video_input, sd_cx25840 and the i2c subdevices set up by the caller). Postcondition: this is cx231xx_register_analog_devices. It logs the driver version, sets dev->norm to V4L2_STD_PAL, dev->width and dev->height from the norm, dev->interlaced to 0 and dev->format to the first format, selects the initial input with video_mux and sets the standard on all subdevices, initialises the video and radio control handlers (10 and 5 controls) and, if dev->sd_cx25840 exists, adds that subdevice's controls to both. If either control handler has a non-zero error it returns that error at once, before any device node is created. It then fills in the video device, and with CONFIG_MEDIA_CONTROLLER initialises its media pad (a failure of media_entity_pads_init is only logged), sets up the video vb2 queue and returns the error of vb2_queue_init if it fails, sets the device capabilities (adding V4L2_CAP_TUNER for the listed boards or when tuner_type is not TUNER_ABSENT) and registers it with video_register_device, returning its error if non-zero. It then does the same for the VBI device (queue, capabilities, media pad, registration), returning the error of vb2_queue_init or video_register_device. If cx231xx_boards[dev->model].radio.type is CX231XX_RADIO it initialises and registers the radio device, returning the error of video_register_device if it fails. It returns 0 if everything succeeded. A failure at any step returns directly without unregistering the device nodes registered by earlier steps and without freeing the control handlers. It takes no locks itself.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is cx231xx_register_analog_devices (cx231xx-video.c:1754-1921), not cx231xx_initdev. Old prose omitted the early return on control-handler errors (before any registration) and the setup of norm/format/input. Mechanical reviewer right about the name.

name: anysee_frontend_attach
prose: Precondition: adap is a valid dvb_usb_adapter whose private anysee_state (hw, has_tda18212, has_ci) and whose dvb_usb_device d with a usable i2c_adap are initialised. Postcondition: this is anysee_frontend_attach. It switches on state->hw and, for each known board variant, does the board's register writes with anysee_wr_reg_mask (the first non-zero result is returned at once, skipping the rest and the final NULL check, and frontends already attached stay in adap->fe[]) and attaches the demodulator for adap->fe[0]; the dual-frontend variants ANYSEE_HW_507FA (E30 Combo Plus) and ANYSEE_HW_508TC / ANYSEE_HW_508PTC (E7 TC and PTC) then do more writes and attach a second demodulator for adap->fe[1] only if adap->fe[0] was attached, without checking whether the second attach succeeded. For ANYSEE_HW_507FA it first probes for the TDA18212 tuner with an I2C transfer at address 0x60 (a failed transfer just means not found; its result is not returned) and sets state->has_tda18212 when it reads 0xc7, which selects the TDA18212 variant of the demodulator configurations and sets the frontend's i2c_gate_ctrl hook. For ANYSEE_HW_508TC, 508PTC, 508S2, 508PS2 and 508T2C it sets state->has_ci to true (for 508TC and 508PTC after the second attach attempt). After the switch it returns -ENODEV, after logging an unsupported-version error, if adap->fe[0] is NULL (including a hw value not listed in the switch); otherwise it returns 0 (the value of ret from the last register write, which is 0 if none was done or all succeeded), even when the optional adap->fe[1] could not be attached.
note: Reviewer right: the second-frontend attach result is not checked (anysee.c:843-859, 900-907), so 0 can be returned with adap->fe[1] NULL; the old prose claimed both frontends were attached. Slice cut the head; function at 697-955. Read fully.

name: az6007_i2c_xfer
prose: Precondition: adap is an i2c_adapter backed by this device, msgs is an array of num valid i2c_msg entries with valid buffers, and the message lengths fit the device's st->data buffer (there is no bounds check against it). Postcondition: it takes st->mutex with mutex_lock_interruptible and returns -EAGAIN without processing anything if that fails. It then handles the messages in order, with i advancing past the read when a pair is merged. A one-byte write followed by a read at the same address is merged into one AZ6007_I2C_RD request through __az6007_read; the result is converted: if __az6007_read returns at least the requested read length the data is copied from st->data into the read buffer, otherwise (including when __az6007_read returned a negative error) the status becomes -EIO. A write message with length 0 returns -EIO; any other write sends its first byte as the index and the remaining bytes as data through __az6007_write, whose result is the status. A read message with length 0 returns -EIO; any other read calls __az6007_read and copies len bytes from st->data into the buffer whatever the status (so a failed read copies stale data), and the status is the return of __az6007_read, so a short but non-negative read is not treated as an error here. As soon as a status is negative it stops processing and, after releasing st->mutex, logs it and returns that negative status. If all messages are processed without a negative status it releases st->mutex and returns num (also when num is 0), not the byte counts from the reads.
note: Reviewer 1 wrong: positive read byte counts are not returned; the function returns num on success (az6007.c:833). Reviewer 3 mixed: in the merged path read failures and short reads become -EIO (780-784, right), but in the non-merged read path the error of __az6007_read is returned as is and a short non-negative read is not an error (818-824, wrong). Old prose missed the data copy on failed plain reads. az6007_i2c_xfer at 743-834.

name: mxl111sf_i2c_xfer
prose: Precondition: adap is a valid i2c_adapter whose adapter data is a dvb_usb_device with a valid mxl111sf_state in d->priv, and msg contains num valid i2c_msg entries. Postcondition: it takes d->i2c_mutex with mutex_lock_interruptible and returns -EAGAIN, processing nothing, if that is interrupted. Otherwise it transfers the messages in order, using the hardware I2C engine (mxl111sf_i2c_hw_xfer_msg) when state->chip_rev is above MXL111SF_V6 and the software bit-banged transfer (mxl111sf_i2c_sw_xfer_msg) otherwise; it stops at the first message for which the helper reports a failure (mxl_fail), logs a debug message, releases the mutex and returns -EREMOTEIO whatever the helper's error code was. If all num messages succeed it releases the mutex and returns num (0 for num == 0). It keeps no memory or reference.
note: Reviewer 4 wrong for this function: the final return is 'i == num ? num : -EREMOTEIO' (mxl111sf-i2c.c:827), so a failed message yields -EREMOTEIO; the -EIO the reviewer saw is set inside the lower-level helpers, not here. mxl111sf_i2c_xfer at 799-828.

name: seqhead_to_package
prose: Precondition: go is a valid go7007 (sensor_framerate, fps_scale and interlace_coding set so that vti_bitlen and the fps division are valid, fps_scale non-zero), code points to a buffer of space __le16 words, and sequence_header_func is a valid callback that fills the 40-byte local buffer with at most 40 bytes of sequence header and returns a length (the function does not check that length). Postcondition: it computes the VOP time-increment bit length and the frame rate (doubled for interlace coding), calls sequence_header_func(go, buf, 1) on a zero-initialised 40-byte buffer, and builds a local table of 50 (register, value) pairs, 100 words, whose non-zero entries are three packages' worth: frame-rate and time-increment registers, then registers 0xc800-0xc803 from buf[2..9], 0xc406 = 64, 0xc407 = len - 64 (stored as a 16-bit value, with no check that len is at least 64) and 0xc61b = 1, then registers 0xc808-0xc815 from buf[10..37]; the remaining pairs are zero. It returns copy_packages(code, pack, 3, space): if space is less than 96 it returns -1 and writes nothing; otherwise it writes the first 96 words (three 32-word packages, i.e. the first 48 pairs, converted to little-endian) into code and returns 96. The last two pairs of the local table are not copied. No locks are taken and no allocations are made.
note: Reviewer 1 right (buf is 40 bytes and c407 is len - 64 with no check that len >= 64); reviewer 2/3 partly right: the table has 50 pairs (not 51), of which only 48 pairs/96 words are copied by copy_packages(…, 3, …) (go7007-fw.c:277-288), and about 30 pairs are non-zero. Old prose said 'a negative error code' for failure; copy_packages returns exactly -1. seqhead_to_package at 1198-1263.

name: do_special
prose: Precondition: go points to an initialised go7007 device, code points to a buffer with space free 16-bit words, framelen points to a writable int (used by the MPEG frame-header and bit-rate-control builders), and type is a u16 firmware special code. Postcondition: it dispatches on type. SPECIAL_FRM_HEAD calls gen_mjpeghdr_to_package for go->format V4L2_PIX_FMT_MJPEG, gen_mpeg1hdr_to_package for MPEG1 or MPEG2, gen_mpeg4hdr_to_package for MPEG4, and for any other format falls out of the switch. SPECIAL_BRC_CTRL calls brctrl_to_package, SPECIAL_CONFIG config_package, SPECIAL_AV_SYNC avsync_to_package, SPECIAL_FINAL final_package, SPECIAL_AUDIO audio_to_package and SPECIAL_MODET modet_to_package. SPECIAL_SEQHEAD calls seqhead_to_package with the MPEG1 or MPEG4 sequence-header callback for MPEG1/MPEG2 and MPEG4 formats, and returns 0 with nothing written for any other format. In every dispatched case the builder's return value is returned unchanged (words written, or its negative failure value) without any logging here, and words the builder wrote before failing may remain in code. If type is not one of the SPECIAL_* codes, or type is SPECIAL_FRM_HEAD with an unsupported go->format, no builder is called, it logs 'firmware file contains unsupported feature' with dev_err and returns -1. It takes no locks.
note: Reviewer 1 right (SPECIAL_FRM_HEAD with an unsupported format returns -1 with no builder called, go7007-fw.c:1509-1512 then 1538-1540); reviewer 3 right (a builder failure is returned directly, without dev_err and not converted to -1). The old prose lumped builder failure with the logged -1 cases. do_special at 1494-1541.

name: sd_callback
prose: Precondition: gspca_dev points to a struct gspca_dev that is the first member of a struct sd (sd->sensor, nbRightUp, mirrorMask, waitSet and dev_camera_settings set at probe; nbRightUp starts at 1). Postcondition: the function returns nothing. _OV9655_ is a run-time test (sd->sensor == ID_OV9655), not a preprocessor symbol. If sd->sensor is not ID_OV9655 it reads one byte with ctrl_in(0xc0, 2, 0x0000, ...) into a local 'state' whose value is unspecified if the read fails (the return value is ignored), treats 0xc8 or 0x40 as upside-down and any other value as right-up, and updates the orientation counter: for an upside-down reading, only if nbRightUp > -4, it first sets a positive nbRightUp to 0, sets mirrorMask to 1 and waitSet to 1 if nbRightUp is exactly -3, and then decrements nbRightUp; for a right-up reading, only if nbRightUp < 4, it first sets a negative nbRightUp to 0, sets mirrorMask to 0 and waitSet to 1 if nbRightUp is exactly 3, and then increments it. So nbRightUp stays within [-4, 4]; the mirror change is assigned (not toggled) and the change takes effect after three consecutive right-up readings from the initial value 1 or four consecutive upside-down readings from 0. If sd->sensor is ID_OV9655 no read is done and nbRightUp and mirrorMask are not touched. In all cases, if sd->waitSet is non-zero it then calls sd->dev_camera_settings(gspca_dev); this function never clears waitSet.
note: Reviewer 1 right (the _OV9655_ test skips the probe; upside-down needs four readings; mirrorMask is assigned); reviewer 2 right (from the initial nbRightUp = 1, gl860.c:327, the right-up change triggers on the third reading); reviewer 3 right (_OV9655_ is the expression ((struct sd*)gspca_dev)->sensor == ID_OV9655 in gl860.h:26, so 'defined/not defined' was wrong). sd_callback at 459-496.

name: gspca_init_transfer
prose: Precondition: gspca_dev points to an initialized gspca device that is not currently streaming, whose USB interface is claimed and whose cam, iface and xfer_ep fields have been set by the caller. Postcondition: it returns the negative error of sd_desc->isoc_init, or -EIO when no endpoint is found for the forced altsetting or build_isoc_ep_tb yields no entry (in these early failures the input URB and the streaming state are untouched); otherwise gspca_input_destroy_urb has been called and gspca_input_create_urb is called before every later return, and it returns a non-negative value on success with gspca_dev->streaming true and the transfer URBs created and submitted (no URBs are created if cam.no_urb_create is set, and none are submitted if cam.bulk && cam.bulk_nurbs == 0, the subdriver having started the bulk transfer itself), or a negative errno from usb_set_interface, create_urbs, sd_desc->start, sd_desc->isoc_nego or usb_submit_urb, or -EIO when the alternate-setting table is exhausted, in which case streaming is false and the URBs are destroyed (by destroy_urbs, or by gspca_stream_off after a failed usb_submit_urb); a -ENOSPC from usb_set_interface or usb_submit_urb does not return but retries after msleep(20) with sd_desc->isoc_nego or the next lower alternate setting, returning -EIO if no lower setting remains. In the failure case after usb_set_interface fails (other than -ENOSPC) no URBs exist at that point (they are created after that call, or were already destroyed by gspca_stream_off on an earlier retry), so no destroy call is needed. gspca_dev->streaming is set to true only after sd_desc->start succeeds and before the URBs are submitted.
note: Checked every return and goto against gspca.c:756-897. The only reviewer complaint concerned an old annotation claiming URBs are destroyed on the usb_set_interface error path; the code goes straight to 'out' (816-821) but no URBs exist then, which the added sentence states. Prose otherwise unchanged and correct. Slice cut the head.

name: cit_start_model1
prose: Precondition: gspca_dev points to a valid, initialised gspca_dev that is the first member of a struct sd, whose pixfmt.width is set (128, 176 or 352 select the resolution-specific register writes in two switches; any other width skips them), and cit_get_clock_div(gspca_dev) can compute a divider. Postcondition: if cit_get_clock_div returns a negative value the function returns that value at once without touching the device. Otherwise it runs a fixed model-1 start-up sequence of register reads and writes (cit_read_reg, cit_write_reg) and packet writes in both formats (cit_Packet_Format1 and cit_PacketFormat2, some of them repeated cit_model1_ntries times), toggling the LED register 0x0100 several times along the way, applies the resolution-specific register values for width 128, 176 or 352 twice (the second time as the 'assorted init' block), and finally writes 0x01 to register 0x0100 (LED on) and the computed clock divider to register 0x0111, and returns 0. The two blocks under 'if (0)' (default brightness, contrast, sharpness and lighting writes) are never executed. The results of the register reads and writes are not checked. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer 4 partly wrong: cit_PacketFormat2 is called unconditionally many times (xirlink_cit.c:1575-1602); only the brightness/contrast/sharpness/lighting block (1613-1621 and 1671-1691) is inside if (0) and never runs. The old prose was right to mention cit_PacketFormat2 but did not say that the width switches are applied twice or that register results are ignored. cit_start_model1 at 1531-1731 (slice cut the head); read fully.

name: hdpvr_read
prose: Precondition: *pos is 0 (otherwise the function returns -ESPIPE without touching the device) and buffer can accept up to count bytes. Postcondition: returns the number of bytes copied (possibly 0 when count is 0 or when the next buffer is not ready and the device is disconnected), or a negative errno when no bytes were copied: -ESPIPE if *pos is nonzero; -EIO if hdpvr_start_streaming fails on an idle device (the mutex is released, the device sleeps 200 ms and dev->status is reset to STATUS_IDLE); -ERESTARTSYS if the initial blocking wait for the first buffer is interrupted by a signal (streaming, if started, is left running); -EAGAIN if the file is O_NONBLOCK and the next buffer is not ready and no bytes were copied yet; the negative errno returned by wait_event_interruptible_timeout if that wait is interrupted (this overwrites any partial byte count already accumulated); the error code returned by the restart call to hdpvr_start_streaming after a 1-second buffer timeout (streaming was stopped and the 4-second firmware settle sleep performed); or -EAGAIN at the end of the function if no byte was copied and no buffer was available at all (hdpvr_get_next_buffer returned NULL, which can also happen with count 0), or -EFAULT if copy_to_user fails and no bytes were copied yet (if bytes were already copied, the partial count is returned instead and the copy error is not reported). On success some data has been copied to buffer, streaming has been started if the device was idle (with dev->owner set to the caller's v4l2 file handle), and *pos is not advanced by this function.
note: Reviewers 2 and 3 right (wait and restart errors overwrite a partial byte count: ret = err at hdpvr-video.c:463 and 480, then 'goto err'); the old prose already said it for the wait error and I now rely on it for the restart error too. Added the missing -EAGAIN at the end (524-526: '!ret && !buf'). Checked all returns/gotos of hdpvr_read at 410-528; the rest of the old prose (ESPIPE, EIO after 200 ms sleep and dev->status reset, ERESTARTSYS, EFAULT partial count) matches the code.

name: state_eval_encoder_config
prose: Precondition: hdw points to a valid, initialised pvr2_hdw whose encoder_wait_timer is initialised and which is not being modified concurrently by the caller's state-machine peers. Postcondition: the return value is 0 when no state bit was changed (or the function is only waiting) and non-zero when a state bit was changed or the encoder was configured. Case A (state_encoder_config is set): if state_encoder_ok is set, state_pipeline_req is set and state_pipeline_pause is clear it returns 0 and changes nothing; otherwise it clears state_encoder_config and state_encoder_waitok, calls timer_delete_sync on the wait timer and returns non-zero. Case B (state_encoder_config is clear): if any of these fails: state_pathway_ok, pathway_state == PVR2_PATHWAY_ANALOG, state_encoder_ok, state_pipeline_idle, state_pipeline_pause clear, state_pipeline_req, state_pipeline_config, then it deletes the wait timer if it is pending, and returns non-zero after clearing state_encoder_waitok if that flag was set, or returns 0 if it was already clear. If all those conditions hold and state_encoder_waitok is clear, it returns 0 after starting encoder_wait_timer (for TIME_MSEC_ENCODER_WAIT ms) if the timer was not pending and the flag is still clear on a second check, or returns 0 without any change if the timer is already pending or the flag became set. If all conditions hold and state_encoder_waitok is set, it calls pvr2_encoder_configure, sets state_encoder_config only if state_encoder_ok is still set afterwards, and returns non-zero in every case, even if no state bit changed because the configure left state_encoder_ok clear.
note: Reviewer 1 right (non-zero returned after pvr2_encoder_configure even when state_encoder_ok stays false and no bit changes, pvrusb2-hdw.c:4302-4306); reviewer 2 right (the wait timer can be deleted with no flag change, 4268-4270); reviewer 3 right (returns 0 when the timer is already pending or the flag becomes set, 4282-4300). The old prose merged these into one hard-to-read sentence; rewritten as cases. state_eval_encoder_config at 4245-4307.

name: ttusb_dec_process_urb_frame
prose: Precondition: dec points to a valid ttusb_dec decoder state and b points to length bytes that are both readable and writable (swap_bytes swaps each adjacent pair in place; with an odd length the last byte is not swapped); length is non-negative. Postcondition: it swaps the bytes of b, then consumes all length bytes in a loop driven by dec->packet_state, a state machine that survives across calls. States 0 to 2 look for three 0xaa bytes (any other byte resets the state to 0); state 3 accepts 0x00 (setting packet_length to 0 and moving on), stays at 3 on 0xaa and resets to 0 on any other byte; state 4 collects two bytes into dec->packet and sets packet_type to PVA for 'AV', SECTION for a first byte 'S', or EMPTY for a first byte 0x00 (payload length 2, going to state 7), and for any other pair prints 'unknown packet type' with printk and resets the state to 0; state 5 collects header bytes until 8 (PVA) or 5 (SECTION) bytes are present and computes packet_payload_length from the header; state 6 copies payload bytes (as many as are available, up to the remaining payload) into dec->packet; state 7 collects the trailing bytes (4, or 5 for a SECTION packet with an odd payload length) one at a time and, when packet_length reaches payload_length + tail, calls ttusb_dec_process_packet(dec) and resets the state to 0. Any other value of packet_state prints 'illegal packet state encountered' with printk and resets the state to 0 without consuming a byte. Partial packet state stays in dec for the next call. The function returns nothing; it does not itself check packet_length against the size of dec->packet and takes no locks.
note: Reviewer 2 right (the unknown-packet-type message is printed in this function, ttusb_dec.c:691-694); reviewer 3 wrong (the default case does print and reset, 762-765, and the reset avoids a loop); reviewer 1 right in the original (writable buffer). I dropped the old claims about what ttusb_dec_process_packet prints and dispatches because I did not read that function. ttusb_dec_process_urb_frame at 641-768.

name: usbtv_image_chunk
prose: Precondition: usbtv is a valid initialised usbtv device (n_chunks, frame_id, chunks_done, last_odd, sequence, buflock and the bufs list set up) and chunk points to at least 241 readable 32-bit words (964 bytes: a header word followed by 240 words of data, which usbtv_chunk_to_vbuf reads as two halves of 120 words), even though the caller steps through its data buffer in USBTV_CHUNK_SIZE (256) byte increments. Postcondition: it returns without changing anything if the header magic is bad or the chunk number is at least usbtv->n_chunks. Otherwise, when the chunk number is 0 it sets usbtv->frame_id to the chunk's frame id and usbtv->chunks_done to 0 (before comparing frame ids), and it then returns without further action if usbtv->frame_id differs from the chunk's frame id. Otherwise it takes usbtv->buflock with spin_lock_irqsave (released on every path) and returns if usbtv->bufs is empty. Otherwise it takes the first buffer without removing it, copies the chunk data into the buffer's plane with usbtv_chunk_to_vbuf and increments usbtv->chunks_done. If the chunk number is n_chunks - 1 it then, when the odd flag is set and usbtv->last_odd was clear, sets the buffer's field to V4L2_FIELD_INTERLACED, its sequence to usbtv->sequence (which it increments), its timestamp to ktime_get_ns(), its plane 0 payload to the plane size, calls vb2_buffer_done with VB2_BUF_STATE_DONE if usbtv->chunks_done equals n_chunks and VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR otherwise, and removes the buffer from usbtv->bufs with list_del after that call. For the last chunk it always sets usbtv->last_odd to the odd flag, whether or not the buffer was completed. It releases the lock and returns nothing.
note: Reviewers 1 and 2 right (frame-id check, and chunk_no 0 updates frame_id/chunks_done before it; old prose already said so); reviewer 3 right: the data copy reads 240 words after the header (USBTV_CHUNK = 240, usbtv_chunk_to_vbuf at usbtv-video.c:379-393), so the 256-byte precondition was wrong. Corrections in order: vb2_buffer_done is called before list_del (452-453) and last_odd is set for every last chunk, also when no buffer is completed (455). usbtv_image_chunk at 398-459.

name: uvc_ctrl_set
prose: Precondition: the caller holds chain->ctrl_mutex (a lockdep assertion), handle->chain is valid, and for a compound mapping xctrl->ptr points to xctrl->size bytes of readable user memory. Postcondition: it returns -EACCES if xctrl->id is a V4L2 control class id, -EINVAL if uvc_find_control finds no control for xctrl->id, and -EACCES if that control lacks UVC_CTRL_FLAG_SET_CUR. It then calls uvc_ctrl_clamp on xctrl->value: for integer, bitmask and boolean mappings that call (which may first populate the control cache and return its negative error) rewrites xctrl->value in place with the clamped value (rounded to the step and clamped to min/max, masked with the bitmap, or limited to 0 or 1); for menu mappings it leaves xctrl->value unchanged and returns -ERANGE if the index is outside the range of bits set in mapping->menu_mask, -EINVAL if the index is not set in the mask or, for bitmask-typed controls, not allowed by the control's bitmap; for other types it does nothing; a non-zero result is returned at once. If the mapping does not span the whole UVC control (control size * 8 differs from mapping->size) it loads the current value with __uvc_ctrl_load_cur and returns its negative error. If ctrl->dirty is 0 it copies the CURRENT data to BACKUP (so BACKUP changes even if the next step fails). It then stores the new value into CURRENT: for a non-compound mapping with uvc_mapping_set_s32 from xctrl->value (cannot fail), for a compound mapping by checking that xctrl->size equals the mapping's size (-EINVAL otherwise), copying the user data with memdup_user (its error returned) and calling mapping->set (its result returned). On a failure at that step it returns the error, leaving ctrl->dirty and ctrl->modified as they were at entry. On success it sets ctrl->dirty and ctrl->modified to 1 and returns 0. The caller keeps chain->ctrl_mutex.
note: Reviewer 1 right (BACKUP is overwritten before the store can fail, uvc_ctrl.c:2611-2619); reviewer 2 right (a compound control is stored from xctrl->ptr with size check and memdup_user, 2543-2564); reviewer 3 right (uvc_ctrl_clamp rewrites *value_in_out only for integer, bitmask and boolean types, 2493, 2504, 2508; menu and default return without touching it). The old prose also missed the extra -EINVAL for bitmask-typed menu values (2531-2532). uvc_ctrl_set at 2578-2624, callees at 2460-2576.

name: uvc_probe_video
prose: Precondition: stream is a valid initialised UVC streaming interface (stream->dev, stream->intf, stream->maxpsize set) and probe points to a caller-owned uvc_streaming_control holding the requested parameters. Postcondition: it sends the probe with uvc_set_video_ctrl(SET_CUR) and returns a negative result at once. If the device does not have UVC_QUIRK_PROBE_MINMAX it reads GET_MIN and GET_MAX into local structures (returning a negative result at once) and sets probe->wCompQuality to the maximum's wCompQuality. It then runs at most two rounds of: SET_CUR of probe, then GET_CUR into probe (overwriting it with the device's values), each negative result being returned at once; after the GET_CUR it stops with a result of 0 if the interface has a single alternate setting or if probe->dwMaxPayloadTransferSize is not above stream->maxpsize. If the payload is too large and UVC_QUIRK_PROBE_MINMAX is set it returns -ENOSPC. Otherwise it overwrites probe->wKeyFrameRate, wPFrameRate and wCompWindowSize with the minimum values and wCompQuality with the maximum value and goes on to the next round. If both rounds end without the payload fitting (and the quirk is clear) it returns 0, with probe holding those substituted values rather than the last GET_CUR result and dwMaxPayloadTransferSize possibly still above stream->maxpsize. The specific negative errors of the SET_CUR/GET_CUR/GET_MIN/GET_MAX helpers are passed through unchanged. It allocates nothing itself and takes no locks.
note: Reviewer 1 right (success does not guarantee the payload fits, 468-481); reviewer 2 right (after two unsuccessful rounds probe is overwritten after the last GET_CUR, 477-480); reviewer 3 right (-ENOSPC is returned despite successful transfers when the quirk is set, 471-473). I removed the old claim listing -ENOMEM/-EIO/-EPROTO since those come from the helpers I did not read. uvc_probe_video at 426-485.
